ig_carousel_topic.topic: What 'units' actually mean (and why win % alone is a lie)
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Your buddy says he's 60% on the season.
He's still down money.
Here's why.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors track wins and losses.
That number feels good. It means almost nothing.
A 60% record betting -200 favorites loses money fast.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Units measure how much you actually profit per bet risked.
One unit = your standard bet size (say, $50).
A 54% record at -110 odds is worth about +0.8u per 10 bets. That compounds.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Real example:
Bettor A: 60% win rate, all -200 favorites. Net: -2.0u over 20 bets.
Bettor B: 54% win rate, all -110 lines. Net: +1.6u over 20 bets.
Bettor B wins more money. Every time.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Win rate is a vanity stat.
Units won is the scoreboard.
SmarterPicks: 271-229, +47.0u, 9.3% ROI this year. That's the number that pays.
